maya (ml): FYI ran a focused KV-cache quantization run comparing FP8-KV vs INT8-KV on rw-13b-v2. curious about the latency tail and memory tradeoffs.

maya (ml): Setup: long-chat workload (avg seq 2048, prefix reuse ~40%), batch_size=8, streaming off, kv-cache persisted between calls.

maya (ml): TL;DR — FP8-KV saves ~28% GPU memory, p99 increases ~12-18ms depending on seq, p95 stable; INT8-KV saves ~40% memory but p99 spike larger (~30ms) and occasional token stutter on long ctx. accuracy delta vs fp16: FP8 +0.3% loss on LM-eval (perplexity), INT8 +1.1%.

jon (infra): Can you paste the exact p50/p95/p99 numbers and memory numbers?

maya (ml): Sure — full run below (single A100-80GB instance):

maya (ml): ```
model: rw-13b-v2
mode: kv-quant (fp16 baseline; fp8-kv; int8-kv)
workload: long-chat synth (avg seq 2048)
batch: 8
results:
  baseline (fp16): memory=46.2GB, p50=22ms, p95=68ms, p99=110ms, ppl=17.4
  fp8-kv:        memory=33.2GB, p50=23ms, p95=71ms, p99=129ms, ppl=17.5
  int8-kv:       memory=27.5GB, p50=24ms, p95=80ms, p99=140ms, ppl=17.6
notes: fp8 reduced per-token memory for KV but required small dequant step on long chains; int8 was denser but more quant noise on some attention heads
```

maya (ml): Also ran a 4hr stability run; INT8 had 2 brief stutters where token emission lagged ~300-500ms then recovered. FP8 had no stutters, just smoother tail.

tess (bench): Nice. Did you try mixed strategy (fp8 for keys, int8 for values) or per-layer heuristics?

maya (ml): Yes — we experimented with hybrid kv profiles: fp8-keys/int8-values and selective-int8 on bottom 6 layers. Hybrid got memory ~30GB, p99 ~135ms, ppl ~17.55. The best accuracy/latency sweet spot was FP8-KV across all layers.

jon (infra): What about cache hit behavior? If prefix reuse drops, do we see different tails?

maya (ml): Good question. I swept reuse from 20%->60%: FP8 benefits amplify with higher reuse (more saved KV writes), INT8 still saves more absolute mem but the p99 delta vs baseline grows as reuse goes up because quant dequant overhead per KV read becomes more frequent.

ciara-bot: perf-run 1779234567 finished. Artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/runs/1779234567/ (profiles, flamegraphs, raw logs)

jon (infra): Can you include the kernel-level breakdown? Is the p99 from memcpy/quant routines or attention matmul?

maya (ml): Kernel breakdown from the flamegraph: FP8 p99 extra ~9ms on KV dequant path (memory ops + dequant add), INT8 p99 extra ~22ms, and ~4-8ms extra from slightly larger attention reprojection error triggers fallback path in last layers. No network variance — single host.

ops: For deployment risk: what's the observed accuracy regression ceiling? We need guardrails if we roll out to dedicated pools.

maya (ml): On our eval set (conversational QA + code tasks): FP8 worst-case delta +0.6% on exact match for a couple prompts; mean delta +0.3%. INT8 worst-case +1.8%. We flagged 3 prompts with hallucination uptick under INT8.

tess (bench): Any canary suggestion? watchdog metrics?

maya (ml): Canary: start FP8-KV on 5% traffic on a low-latency dedicated pool, monitor p99 latency, token error rate (TER) from eval harness, and prompt-level EM. Thresholds: abort if p99 > baseline p99 + 40ms or TER delta > 0.7% or EM drop > 0.8%.

jon (infra): For Dedicated customers with tight latency SLOs we should default to FP16 or FP8 only on non-critical routes. Also add per-route quant profile toggle in runtime.

maya (ml): Agreed. I'll open a rollout PR with the canary config and attach the run artifacts. Also adding a small regression eval set (10 prompts) to be run as part of canary.

tess (bench): Could you add the quick command so I can repro locally?

maya (ml): repro snippet:```bash
python bench_kv_quant.py --model rw-13b-v2 --mode fp8-kv --batch 8 --seq 2048 --persist-kv true --outdir /tmp/run_fp8
python bench_kv_quant.py --model rw-13b-v2 --mode int8-kv --batch 8 --seq 2048 --persist-kv true --outdir /tmp/run_int8
```

maya (ml): I'll also add the hybrid-profile configs. tagging @jon and @tess for follow-ups. :memo:

jon (infra): LGTM — once PR up, infra will stage pool and enable perf monitoring.

tess (bench): I'll try the repro and run the smaller canary eval overnight.

maya (ml): Thanks — filing follow-ups: 1) PR for canary config + eval suite; 2) notebook with per-layer quant sensitivity; 3) perf dashboard tile for kv-quant p99 breakdown.

maya (ml): cc ops for any policy concerns @ops
